text:
Seton Hall to host community blood drive on October 14 at University Center
A. M. Egan
Seton Hall University will host an American Red Cross Community Blood Drive on October 14, 2026, in the Event Room of the University Center at its South Orange campus. The event is organized by the Buccino Leadership Institute and the Student Nursing Association and is open to students, faculty, staff, and community members from 10 a.m. to 3 p.m.
The blood drive underscores Seton Hall's ongoing commitment to servant leadership and community service. Corporate sponsor Lord Abbett continues its partnership with the university through support for this event as well as other initiatives such as the Lord Abbett Summer Investing High School Course, Financial Literacy Academy, collaboration with Stillman School's Market Research Center, and various shared community impact projects.
Samantha Gizzi, President of the Student Nursing Association and Buccino Leadership Scholar, said,
"Nurses are called to serve, and that calling doesn't begin the day we earn our credentials—it begins right here, right now, on campus. Hosting this blood drive is one of the most direct ways our members can live out that mission while still in school. As a Buccino Scholar, I am especially proud that leadership and service are coming together in an event that could save dozens of lives in our community. I encourage every Pirate to show up, roll up a sleeve and make a difference."
Catherine Tantillo, Global Head of Social Impact at Lord Abbett, said,
"Our partnership with Seton Hall University is grounded in a belief that business can be a force for good, in the classroom and in the community. From the Summer Investing Course and Financial Literacy Academy to our work with the Market Research Center, we are committed to developing the next generation of thoughtful, capable leaders. Supporting the Red Cross through this student-led blood drive reflects that same commitment to community impact. Every pint collected can save up to three lives, and we are proud to stand alongside Seton Hall students as they learn, lead and serve."
The American Red Cross continues to report an urgent nationwide need for blood donations throughout 2026 so hospitals can meet patient demand.
Those interested in volunteering may contact [email protected] with "Volunteer for Blood Drive" as their subject line. Donors must be at least 16 years old (with additional requirements), weigh at least 110 pounds, have not donated whole blood within 56 days, bring valid ID, and complete a medical history form. Walk-ins are welcome but appointments are preferred.
For more information about eligibility or registration details follow @BuccinoLeaders or @SHU_SNA on social media.
